=== WHAT I CONCLUDED, AND ON WHAT EVIDENCE ===

(1) CODE.WZO2-INCOMPLETE is wrong as stated; the artifact's passes=1 coverage is complete and correct. Evidence is a derivation plus an exhaustive measurement, and they were done in that order so the measurement was a prediction test rather than a fishing trip. Derivation from three source facts: passes=1 states have exactly one kind of in-edge, a pass from passes=0 (genChildren4 emits pass at passes+1 and placements at passes=0, exp6_solve.zig:914-942; census seeds only passes=0 roots, :964-969); the pass child is (board, 1-side, KO_NONE, passes+1) (:927); and a passes=0 state is entered only by a placement, which always leaves a stone of the mover's colour (genericPosFromMove writes the stone at :164, removes only opponent chains at :170 guarded by pos[q]*colour<0, and returns error.Suicide at :176). Therefore (P,s,KO_NONE,1) is unreachable exactly when P is monochrome in colour(1-s). Measurement over every group of both shipped artifacts, no sampling: 3x3, 12,675 groups, 1,020 one-sided and 1,020 monochrome, 0 counter-examples in either direction; 4x4, 24,318,165 groups, 131,068 and 131,068, 0 counter-examples in either direction. Independent arithmetic closure: stored passes=1 count equals 2*n_groups minus monochrome count exactly at both sizes (24,330 and 48,505,262, both matching the measured counts).

(2) The census does enumerate pass edges for both sides. Source: the pass child is appended unconditionally before any legality test, for either side (exp6_solve.zig:926-929), and the census's legality filter applies only to passes==0 children (:1011-1015). Artifact test (T266-H2): 0 dropped pass edges and 0 orphans, denominator 48,636,330 side-entries at 4x4.

(3) The genmove miss is a display-path defect in gtp.zig, not artifact incompleteness. bounds2 is called at :1223 AFTER applyMove at :1204, with `side` still naming the mover, so it asks the table about the mover-to-move on the mover's own result. Reproduced at HEAD c344f02 with a freshly built binary. The printed side=1 is the engine i8 side = Black (gtp.zig:168) whereas the key byte uses 0=Black (artifact2.zig:343-345) — that naming collision is why the miss reads as a White-to-move state when it is a Black-to-move one. Established that this is usually silent rather than a miss: after b:B3 w:C2 b:C3 the engine printed [L=16,H=16] where the true state (White to move) is [L=1,H=16], and that is not a colour-inversion of anything.

(4) A1/A2/A8 fail because src/oracle_v2_accept.zig:150-165 carries a second, unfixed copy of the pre-T265 ko rule. Evidence is the checker's own output: all ten sampled A1 refusals (5 per goban size) are at passes=0 with a non-none ko field — none at passes=1, none at ko=none — which directly refutes T261's stated root cause that refusals happen when self-play passes. One traced end to end (3x3 colex=14717, ko=6): the group is present with all four entries at ko=none, and neither white stone adjacent to the captured point satisfies liberties==1 and friendly==0, so the solver correctly stores no ko point while the checker constructs one.

(5) T261's ~6.77M was a colex-ordered prefix reported as a sample. Re-running the first 5,000 groups reproduces its figures to the digit (1,393 one-sided, 27.9%, 8,607 passes=0 and 8,607 passes=1), confirming the selection rule; those groups are stone-count layers 0-4, where monochrome density runs 100/50/25/12.5 percent. True figure 131,068, overstated 51.7x.

(6) Claimlint C7 reads only the first new_rows entry per findings file and mis-parses its status (src/claimlint.zig:1676 and :1716-1718 at HEAD c344f02). Proved by A/B reordering this task's own findings file.

=== INSTRUMENT CALIBRATION (why the zeros are believable) ===
Every counter read zero, which AGENTS.md flags as a red flag in itself. Before believing them: t266_calibrate.py byte-patches synthetic mutants of the 3x3 artifact in a scratch directory (never live data) — a null control plus five seeded defects (dropped pass edge, monochrome-law violation, ko on an occupied cell, passes-bit flip replaying T193, duplicate key byte). Null control clean, all five caught by their targeted counters. Separately, the colex decode the whole result depends on was cross-validated against the Zig implementation in both colours: the engine independently reported colex=12 for its own lone black B3, and the mirror prediction (genmove w must miss at colex 11) was recorded before the run and came out exactly.

=== WHAT I COULD NOT ESTABLISH ===
- A2's 17,136 missing children / 4,224 L/H violations and A8's 5,096 DTT violations are not individually apportioned to the accept-module ko bug. I measured only A1's refusal states. The shared koAfterCapture makes the same cause very likely but I did not demonstrate it; re-running A2/A8 after the fix is the test.
- C-A1 (closure under the move generator) and C-A2 (grounded, no orphans) were specified but not run. They need the Phase 2 kernel. Everything I measured is the structural layer.
- Nothing here tests whether the stored L/H values are correct. That was out of scope and remains untested.
- Whether the solver's ko rule is the RIGHT rule is untouched — that is an axioms question (T271/T275). I established only that exp6_solve.zig, post-T265 gtp.zig and the artifact agree, and that oracle_v2_accept.zig does not.
- I did not establish how many other ko copies diverge. DIRECTION §4.2 says ~14 exist; T265 fixed one, I found a second, and I did not enumerate the rest.

=== WHAT I ASSUMED WITHOUT CHECKING ===
- ENTRY/GROUP ALIGNMENT. Everything rests on entry rows appearing in the same order as the group index, so that starts=cumsum(counts) attributes each entry to the right goban. I never proved this from the writer; I inferred it from oracle_v2_build.zig's loop structure and took C-B4 passing (strict key-byte ascent within every group over 74,814,871 intra-group steps) plus point-lookups agreeing with the engine as corroboration. A systematic off-by-one-group shift would likely have broken C-B4, but I did not construct that mutant, so this is corroborated, not proved.
- SUICIDE SEMANTICS. My F3 depends on genericPosFromMove rejecting suicide, which depends on genericChainCaptured being correct. I read genericPosFromMove and genericIsLegal but NOT genericChainCaptured. If that helper is wrong, the derivation's third leg is weaker than stated — though the exhaustive measurement would then be agreeing with a wrong derivation by coincidence over 24.3M groups, which is implausible but is not the same as checked.
- FULL COLEX UNRANKING. The monochrome classification uses only (layer k, colour_bits), which needs no subset unranking and is the robust part. But the --group renderer and the K3 mutant selection use full combinatorial unranking, which I verified only by eyeball on two positions (3x3 colex 14717 and 4x4 colex 11). I did not round-trip it across a range against src/colex.zig.
- I assumed the DELEGATEE/AGENTS line references I cite are stable enough to be useful, and pinned them to HEAD c344f02 in prose where it mattered. I did not re-resolve every citation I inherited from T261.

=== A GAP I NOTICED AND THEN CLOSED, RECORDED BECAUSE IT NEARLY SHIPPED ===
All my checks are INTERNAL consistency checks. If run_census_4x4 had terminated early (MAX_SWEEPS is 128, exp6_solve.zig:973), whole reachable subtrees would be absent and C-B1/C-B2/H1/H2 would ALL still pass — a truncated BFS drops a passes=0 state and its pass child together, so it produces neither a dropped edge nor an orphan. I had written the conclusion before realising this. Closed it by reading the build log: the 4x4 census terminated naturally at sweep 32 with new_marks=0, far under the cap. The counts also reconcile end to end — census compact states (passes in {0,1}) = 99,133,036 = artifact n_entries exactly, and total reachable 147,638,298 minus compact = 48,505,262 = the passes=1 entry count exactly, which is the bijection between passes=1 states and their passes=2 pass children. This is why C-A1 is the check that actually matters and the C-B layer is only necessary conditions; §5.1 of the evidence doc says so but the reason is this.
